decisions.rationale: Title mention of X-linked amelogenesis imperfecta, a single defined disease form with specific X-linked inheritance and enamel defect rather than a family of diseases. The full span is preferred.
'inherited dental abnormality' is a generic descriptive phrase. The word 'abnormality' is a general term excluded from annotation, so it is not a specific disease name.
Full-form mention of X-linked amelogenesis imperfecta in the abstract. Duplicate mentions are each annotated, even when repeated.
Abbreviation XAI given as the short form of the long-form disease mention. Abbreviation and long form are annotated as separate synonymous mentions.
Standalone use of XAI referring to the disease in 'Three families with XAI'. It is a synonymous mention of the specific disease.
Standalone use of XAI as the disease name in 'linkage was established between XAI and several markers'. It is a specific disease mention.
XAI modifies the noun phrase 'disease process' ('the XAI disease process'), so it functions as a modifier of another concept rather than as a standalone disease mention.
'disease process' is a generic term that refers to a biological process and names no specific disease. General terms and process references are excluded.

Parenthetical AIH1 is used as an alternate designation of the XAI disease entity. It is treated as a synonymous name for a specific disease with no further categorization, annotated as its own mention.
AIH1 is used as the designation of the disease in 'location of AIH1', a specific disease with no further categorization. It is annotated as a repeated mention.
Repeated AIH1 mention in 'AIH1 lies in the interval' referring to the same specific disease designation. Duplicate mentions are annotated.
Repeated AIH1 mention in 'the AIH1 location could not be precisely defined' referring to the same specific disease designation. Duplicate mentions are annotated.
Standalone use of XAI in 'locus heterogeneity in XAI' referring to the specific disease. It is annotated as a synonymous mention of the disease.
